stem: Why is there often a significant delay in diagnosing SCFE when a patient first seeks medical attention?

options.text: Pain is frequently referred to the knee or thigh
X-rays are unable to detect the slip
It is often confused with a common ankle sprain

explanation: Since more than $50\%$ of cases present with knee or thigh pain instead of hip pain, clinicians may focus their investigation on the wrong joint.
rationale: Consider how the nervous system might transmit pain signals from the hip joint to other areas.

optionExplanations.A: Since more than $50\%$ of cases present with knee or thigh pain instead of hip pain, clinicians may focus their investigation on the wrong joint.
optionExplanations.B: Patients typically present with noticeable symptoms such as pain and a limp, though the location of the pain can be misleading.
optionExplanations.C: X-rays are the diagnostic standard, though certain views are better at showing mild slips than others.
optionExplanations.D: While a limp is present, the referred pain to the knee or thigh is the primary reason for diagnostic confusion.

source.hint: Consider how the nervous system might transmit pain signals from the hip joint to other areas.
